title: Mulgore
body: Mulgore is the homeland of the tauren, a sheltered valley of golden grass and gentle hills ringed by mountains on the western edge of the Barrens. The tauren once wandered as nomads, harried by the centaur, until Cairne Bloodhoof, aided by Thrall and his orcs, led his people here, drove the centaur back and claimed the plains. On a towering mesa in the north he raised Thunder Bluff as a refuge for every tribe, and the scattered tribes came together under his rule. Young tauren come of age at Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa and at Bloodhoof Village by Stonebull Lake, proving themselves through the Rites of the Earthmother and the honor of the hunt. Their peace is far from complete. Bristleback quilboar raid from their ravine and even trouble the sacred graves at Red Rocks, Palemane gnolls slaughter the wildlife, Windfury harpies nest along the mountains, dwarves dig into the western hills, and goblins of the Venture Company have poisoned the sacred wells in their hunger for ore.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Mulgore (Warcraft III section: Cairne led the tauren to Mulgore with Thrall's help, centaur driven back, Thunder Bluff founded as a refuge for every tribe, tribes united; enemies of the WoW era)

title: Camp Narache
body: Camp Narache stands at the northern edge of Red Cloud Mesa, high above the plains of southern Mulgore, and here young tauren take their first steps toward adulthood. Chief Hawkwind presides over the camp and reminds every eager newcomer that eagerness is no substitute for wisdom. His son Grull sends novices out to hunt for the tribe's meat, feathers and pelts, while trainers of warriors, hunters, druids and shamans gather in the camp to guide those who follow each path. Seer Ravenfeather readies young shamans for the call of the earth, and the warrior Harutt Thunderhorn teaches that his kind are the ones called upon to defend the borders, hunt the centaur and go to war.

title: Red Cloud Mesa
body: Red Cloud Mesa is a high plateau of rolling grassland atop sheer cliffs in the far south of Mulgore. Plainstriders graze across it, mountain cougars prowl the hills to the south, and battleboars trained by the Bristleback quilboar roam out of the ravine to the east to raid the tauren hunting grounds. A water well lies southeast of Camp Narache, and there Greatmother Hawkwind, the chief's aged mother, goes to draw water at her own unhurried pace. Tucked into the hills directly south of the camp is the abode of Seer Graytongue, who sets young tauren their first test of strength. The mesa is a proving ground, and those who pass its trials follow the road down to Bloodhoof Village.

title: Brambleblade Ravine
body: East of Camp Narache, Brambleblade Ravine is the home of the Bristleback quilboar, who have built a makeshift village there and wage a stubborn war on the tauren from it. Bristleback raiders ambush hunting parties and steal from the camp under cover of darkness, their shamans keep a ritual salve of their own making, and their battleboars are trained to viciousness. At the back of the ravine their leader, Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, keeps his own large hut. A dirt-stained map found in the ravine holds a darker secret: plans drawn up by the Bristleback warchief for an extended siege of Camp Narache.

title: Kodo Rock
body: Kodo Rock is a weathered stone monument on Red Cloud Mesa, standing partway along the trail from Camp Narache to Brambleblade Ravine, and it is easily missed by anyone who is not looking for it. A shaman shrine rests in its shadow, restless spirits of red stone wander the ground nearby, and battleboars from the ravine root through the grass around it. The tauren count it holy ground. Here the young shamans of Camp Narache keep the same rite of earth that orc shamans keep at Spirit Rock in Durotar, drinking a sapta that Seer Ravenfeather brews from a salve taken from the Bristleback shamans, and they return with a small stone to be the heart of their first totem.

title: Bloodhoof Village
body: Bloodhoof Village, named for the tribe of Cairne Bloodhoof, sits in the heart of Mulgore within the curve of Stonebull Lake. It is the first true settlement young tauren reach after leaving Red Cloud Mesa, and the busiest place on the plains outside Thunder Bluff. Cairne's son Baine is its chief, and he sends the young against the threats that trouble the land. Zarlman Two-Moons tends the spirits of the village and brews the Water of the Seers before the tribal fire, Mull Thunderhorn crafts totems to purify the wells, and the old hunter Skorn Whitecloud, old in body but fierce in spirit, still counsels young hunters. Tamed kodo are sold here as mounts, and Innkeeper Kauth welcomes every traveler.

title: Stonebull Lake
body: Stonebull Lake is a long, horseshoe-shaped lake that wraps around Bloodhoof Village on three sides, crossed at its narrowest point by the bridge that carries the road north toward Thunder Bluff. Its waters are rich with fish, and Uthan Stillwater teaches the angler's craft from its banks. On the northern shore the Outrunners of Mulgore fell upon a guarded Venture Company caravan and left its wagons burning. Near the village an old rancher, Ahab Wheathoof, frets over his prized puppy Kyle, who has run off again and can be coaxed home only with tender strider meat.

title: Palemane Rock
body: Palemane Rock is a cave cut into the mountains of western Mulgore, the den of the Palemane gnolls, who also make camp south of Bloodhoof Village. The gnolls tan, skin and poach the creatures of Mulgore without restraint, and they have scorned every attempt the tauren made to speak with them. For Baine Bloodhoof that disrespect was the end of patience: words, he decided, were no longer the answer. Among their camps prowls a brute called Snagglespear, and travelers who stray too close are met with snarls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw.

title: Bael'dun Digsite
body: In the hills northwest of Bloodhoof Village, a dwarven expedition has cut a quarry into the earth at the Bael'dun Digsite. Its diggers and appraisers believe secrets lie buried in the land, and they keep histories of their own people close at hand in the camp, chronicles of the awakening of the dwarves, the War of the Three Hammers and the Battle of Grim Batol. The tauren see the dig very differently. To Baine Bloodhoof, hollowing and defiling the land is no way to earn its teachings, and the digging enrages the kodo of Mulgore. The diggers take their name from Bael'dun, the dwarven stronghold at Bael Modan in the Barrens, where the expedition is based.

title: The Sacred Wells
body: Three sacred water wells, named for the Winterhoof, Thunderhorn and Wildmane clans, give water to the people and beasts of Mulgore: Winterhoof southeast of Bloodhoof Village, Thunderhorn to its north, and Wildmane beyond Thunder Bluff. Goblins of the Venture Company, with the hirelings and laborers in their pay, have overrun all three and fouled the water with their poisons. Driving them off is not enough, for a tainted well must be cleansed. The well stones gathered around them are counted among the reagents of the Water of the Seers, and the tauren hold that the waters of Mulgore must flow clean again.

title: The Ravaged Caravan
body: Near the northern shore of Stonebull Lake lie the burned wagons of a Venture Company caravan. It traveled under guard, and the Outrunners, who had already lost two of their number in an earlier battle with the goblins, attacked without hesitation and set it ablaze. They left the supply crates behind, trusting their torches to destroy anything of value, but not every crate burned. The survivors are stamped with the mark of the Venture Co. Mining Division and packed with ore and minerals bound for processing at one of the company's plants. Goblin laborers and taskmasters have since crept back to pick over the wreckage.

title: The Venture Co. Mine
body: The Venture Co. Mine is bored into the eastern mountains of Mulgore, northeast of the Ravaged Caravan. The goblin company was refused mining rights in the tauren homeland and dug anyway, and its workers and supervisors swarm the tunnels hauling ore from the mineral rich hills. Their orders come from high in the company: a letter to the mine presses for better production from Mulgore and sends equipment approved by the company president, Razdunk, along with the newest shredders and the makings of a lumber mill, for the board believes the plains have timber to offer as well. Deep inside, Supervisor Fizsprocket runs the whole operation.

title: The Rolling Plains
body: Southeast of Bloodhoof Village, the Rolling Plains stretch toward the mountains on Mulgore's border with the Barrens. Windfury harpies and their wind witches nest along the mountain edges away from the road, and Ruul Eagletalon of Bloodhoof sends the young against them as a gauge of their skill before they venture beyond Mulgore. The Windfuries are deadly foes whose strength in battle is matched only by their hunger for fresh meat. Prairie wolf alphas roam the grass, swoops wheel overhead, and a few Galak centaur scouts range across the eastern fields of the tauren homeland.

title: The Golden Plains
body: Southeast of Thunder Bluff opens the Golden Plains, a broad basin of grass that the tauren count among the most treasured corners of their homeland and a favored hunting ground. Plainstriders, swoops, prairie wolves and flatland cougars make it a rich country and a dangerous one. Two beasts of ill fame roam its grass: the great cat known as The Rake, and Mazzranache, a strider with demonic red eyes and a venomous bite that has been the bane of hunters for at least two generations.

title: Windfury Ridge
body: Windfury Ridge runs along the mountains of northern Mulgore, northeast of Thunder Bluff, and it belongs to the Windfury harpies. Their matriarchs and sorceresses nest along the heights and swoop down to seize or slay any traveler who strays too near, and the harpy known as Sister Hatelash hunts the northern hills not far to the west. Wolves and prowling cats roam the slopes below, and so does Arra'chea, a mighty kodo whose horn the high chieftain of Thunder Bluff accepts as proof of a young hunter's skill in tracking and the hunt.

title: Red Rocks
body: Red Rocks is a formation of red sandstone east of Thunder Bluff and the most sacred burial ground of the tauren. Only the most valiant are laid to rest there: the warriors who helped found and defend Thunder Bluff, and those who gave their lives for their tribes and chieftains. Their ancestral spirits linger among the stones, and young tauren who have drunk the Water of the Seers come here to receive their blessing. Kodo graze on the slopes around it. Lorekeeper Raintotem keeps watch over the graves, though he is too old to defend them now, and a band of Bristleback interlopers has come to ravage the burial site.

title: Baine Bloodhoof
body: Baine is the son of Cairne Bloodhoof and Tamaala, and chief of Bloodhoof Village. After the Third War, centaur led by Khiragg raided the tauren village and carried him off, and his grieving father lost the will to lead, until the wanderer Rexxar found the centaur camp and brought Baine home. Since then he has served as Cairne's adviser and leads the tribe whenever his father is away. Calm and thoughtful, he holds that the land has been good to the tauren and that respect for it is everything. He teaches that life and death are a circle, sets himself against the dwarves hollowing the western hills, and sends the young against the Palemane gnolls who slaughter Mulgore's beasts.

title: The Hawkwinds
body: The Hawkwind family keeps the hearth of Camp Narache. Chief Hawkwind, an old friend of Baine Bloodhoof, has seen many eager young tauren pass through his camp and warns them that eagerness is no substitute for wisdom and experience. He sends each one toward the Rites of the Earthmother bearing a totem of his own carving, which Baine knows at a glance. His mother, Greatmother Hawkwind, still draws water from the well southeast of the camp, slower than she once was but no less devoted to the tribe, and she teaches that even the humblest task can earn the notice of elders. The chief's son Grull is a hunter who reminds the young that prey is never mere trophy.

title: Mull Thunderhorn
body: Mull Thunderhorn is a mystic of Bloodhoof Village who has taken up the cleansing of Mulgore's sacred wells since the goblins poisoned them. He cannot heal the water alone. The land itself must offer its aid, so he asks for paws, talons, claws and teeth from the creatures of the plains and, through trance and chant, binds their power into totems of cleansing. He feels every offering deeply, his spirit swelling with sadness and with pride at the sacrifice of the beasts, and he says the ancestors of the Thunderhorn clan have spoken to him in dreams. Goblins, he believes, will never learn the difference between contending with the land and living in harmony with it.

title: Morin Cloudstalker
body: Morin Cloudstalker is one of the Outrunners, whose duty is to keep safe those who travel the plains of Mulgore and to punish any who threaten the tauren homeland. He keeps his post on the road east of Bloodhoof Village. After two Outrunners fell in a clash with the Venture Company, Morin's band attacked a goblin caravan near Stonebull Lake and burned it, and the papers later recovered from its crates confirmed his fears of a plot to drive the tauren from their land and plunder it. He answered in the plain way of his people: tauren, he says, are not ones to mince words, and they have other ways of getting a message across.

title: Zarlman Two-Moons
body: Zarlman Two-Moons is the spiritual leader of Bloodhoof Village, and he always seems to sense when a young tauren walking the Rites of the Earthmother is on the way to him. He guides them through the Rite of Vision, teaching that the land is the people's most holy provider. From stones gathered at the water wells and ambercorn fallen beneath Mulgore's great trees, he brews the Water of the Seers, chanting as he mixes the reagents before the tribal fire. Those who drink it see a vision take shape before the flames, and must follow wherever it leads.

title: Ghost Howl
body: Ghost Howl is a massive white wolf who roams the plains about the foot of Thunder Bluff. The tauren once respected him for his part in the battles against the Burning Legion, but a demon dealt him a terrible wound that never healed, and its torment has turned him against the tauren and their allies. Now he lives out his last days alone in Mulgore, his ragged hide still bearing the demon's wound. In Bloodhoof Village the old hunter Skorn Whitecloud can scarcely believe his eyes when anyone brings proof of the great wolf's death, and hopes that Ghost Howl's spirit has at last found peace.

title: Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle
body: Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the Bristleback quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine, and under him the tribe wages an unending war on the tauren of Red Cloud Mesa. His raiders ambush hunting parties, steal from Camp Narache by night and train their battleboars to savagery, and his people have gone so far as to plan a siege of the camp. Sharptusk himself keeps to a large hut at the back of the ravine, in the heart of his tribe's makeshift village. Others have gone after him and failed. To the braves of the mesa he is the finest kind of quarry, one cunning enough to hunt the hunter back.

title: Supervisor Fizsprocket
body: Supervisor Fizsprocket runs the Venture Company's operation in Mulgore from inside the company mine in the eastern hills. The plains are his jurisdiction, and his superiors expect results. A letter from his superiors reminds him, at President Razdunk's bidding, of the company's ambitions across Kalimdor, notes that its drilling and mining outposts in the Barrens already turn a profit, and presses him for production numbers that have yet to arrive. The board has still approved the equipment he requisitioned, and the tauren name him the mastermind behind the company's plans to drive them from their land so that it might be plundered at will.

title: Mazzranache
body: Mazzranache is a strider of dark reputation that stalks the Golden Plains. Maur Raincaller of Bloodhoof Village grew up on his grandfather's tales of battles with the beast: its demonic red eyes, its razor-sharp talons and its venomous bite. Crossing the plains, Maur met it himself, and it tore a nasty bite from his shoulder that left him burning with fever and lost in delirious nightmares, until a remedy of wolf heart, cougar bone, plainstrider scale and swoop gizzard checked the infection and began to cure it. He will never forget its screeching call, nor the blaze of color as its beak came down upon him.

title: Trials of Red Cloud Mesa
body: A young tauren earns a place in the tribe through deeds, and Camp Narache offers plenty. Grull Hawkwind first sends novices after plainstriders for meat and feathers, then after the mountain cougars of the southern hills, whose pelts clothe the children and mend the tents, and at last against the battleboars the Bristlebacks have trained to raid the hunting grounds, whose snouts and flanks make stew for the young. Brave Windfeather asks for something harder, the head of Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, and a dirt-stained map taken from the ravine reveals the Bristleback plan for a siege of the camp, giving Chief Hawkwind time to call for help from Bloodhoof Village. Not every trial is fought. Antur Fallow, worn out in the middle of his own Rite of Strength, begs someone to carry his father's furs down to the inn at Bloodhoof, where they will become blankets for weary travelers.

title: Rites of the Earthmother
body: The Rites of the Earthmother are the steps by which a young tauren earns the respect of the elders of Thunder Bluff. They begin with a humble task, a pitcher of water carried from Greatmother Hawkwind's well, for even the smallest service can win an elder's notice. Chief Hawkwind then sends the youth to Seer Graytongue for the Rite of Strength, a test of bravery against the Bristlebacks of Brambleblade Ravine, and afterward down the road to Bloodhoof Village with a totem of his carving for Baine Bloodhoof. In the Rite of Vision, Zarlman Two-Moons brews the Water of the Seers from well stones and ambercorn, and the drinker follows a howling vision across the plains to Seer Wiserunner. The Rite of Wisdom ends at Red Rocks, where the ancestral spirits of those who died founding and defending Thunder Bluff pass their duty of protection to the young tauren, who may then enter the city with pride and present themselves to Cairne Bloodhoof.

title: The Poisoned Wells
body: When the Venture Company's goblins and their servants fouled the sacred wells of Mulgore, Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village set out to heal them, one at a time. Each well needs its own totem of cleansing, and each totem demands an offering from the land. For the Winterhoof well southeast of the village he took the paws of prairie wolves and the talons of plainstriders. For the Thunderhorn well to the north he took the claws of stalkers and cougars, whose purity in the hunt he holds vital to the work. For the Wildmane well, last and farthest, beyond Thunder Bluff, he needed the teeth of prairie wolf alphas, and felt the sacrifice keenly. At each well the totem must be carried past the goblins and a ritual performed. As each is cleansed, the beasts return to drink, the Thunderhorn ancestors give thanks in a dream, and Mull prays that the waters of Mulgore may stay clean forever.
sources: quests 748, 754, 756, 758, 759, 760 (descriptions and reward texts)

title: The Venture Company in Mulgore
body: The Outrunners had already lost two of their own to the Venture Company when they found a goblin caravan traveling under guard near Stonebull Lake. They burned it and moved on, but salvagers were soon seen picking through the wreck, and Morin Cloudstalker sent someone to look. The surviving crates held ore and minerals stamped for the company's Mining Division, along with a sheaf of documents granting Supervisor Fizsprocket equipment approved by President Razdunk and urging greater production from the mineral rich plains. The company had been refused mining rights in Mulgore and was taking the ore anyway. Morin's answer was blunt. Workers and supervisors in the mine northeast of the caravan were struck down to send the goblins a message, and Fizsprocket, mastermind of the plans to drive the tauren from their land, was slain in his mine and his clipboard carried back for study.
sources: quests 749, 751, 764, 765 (descriptions, request and reward texts)

title: Sharing the Land
body: Baine Bloodhoof teaches that the land has been good to the tauren and must be respected in return, and two intruders in Mulgore have refused that lesson. To the south and west, the Palemane gnolls kill the creatures of the plains without restraint and have scorned every attempt to speak with them, so Baine sends the young to cut down their tanners, skinners and poachers, so that they may see how terrible even a small threat to the land can become if left unchecked. Death and life, he reminds them afterward, are a circle, and neither can exist without the other. To the northwest, dwarves are hollowing the hills at the Bael'dun Digsite in search of the earth's secrets, and their digging enrages the kodo. There Baine asks not for blood but for their tools: picks taken from the dig and smashed at a forge, in the hope that the dwarves learn that hollowing the land is not the path to knowledge.
